project_overview: This project appears to be a web application likely related to student management, focusing on academic records and potentially exam results. The codebase demonstrates a component-based architecture with various Vue.js components interacting with backend services. There's a significant amount of code imported between components, suggesting a complex system. Several files are deeply intertwined, potentially creating maintenance challenges.

layers.description: Core business logic and data handling.
Small, reusable functions, likely for testing and linting.

macro_trends.title: Deep Component Dependencies
macro_trends.description: Multiple Vue.js components heavily import each other, potentially leading to a brittle architecture and difficulties in understanding the flow of data and logic. This creates a high risk of cascading changes and debugging complexity.

macro_trends.title: Prop Drilling
macro_trends.description: The extensive import and re-use of components suggests significant prop drilling to pass data down the component tree. This can lead to performance issues and make it difficult to reason about the data flow.

macro_trends.title: Circular Dependency Chains
macro_trends.description: The import/export relationships between 'login.spec.js', 'test.js', and '.eslintrc.js'  represent a circular dependency chain.  This can cause unpredictable behaviour during testing and build processes.

key_workflows.name: User Login Workflow
key_workflows.description: The login process involves multiple components, from the initial display of the login form to the underlying service calls to authenticate users. This workflow is heavily reliant on props being passed down to different components.

key_workflows.name: Student Data Retrieval Workflow
key_workflows.description: Retrieving and displaying student data (e.g., profile, marksheet) involves the interaction of the Frontend components with the 'mql.js' backend service. The architecture is heavily dependent on data being fetched and transformed efficiently.
